title: Compare With the Previous Row
story: LAG looks at the previous row. Use it for day-on-day change.
goal: For each delivered order (ordered by order_date, id) show id, qty and prev_qty (the previous delivered order's qty, NULL for the first).
starter:
SELECT id, qty, NULL AS prev_qty
FROM orders
WHERE status = 'delivered'
ORDER BY order_date, id;

tests.label: Hidden check on other data

hints: LAG(qty) OVER (ORDER BY ...) returns the value from the row above.
The first row has nothing above it, so it is NULL.
SELECT id, qty, LAG(qty) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS prev_qty FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' ORDER BY order_date, id;
socratic: Why is the first prev_qty NULL?
How would you compute the change qty - prev_qty?
explain: In one sentence: what does this query do, and why does it need the LAG?
solution: SELECT id, qty, LAG(qty) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS prev_qty FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' ORDER BY order_date, id;
alt: SELECT id, qty, LAG(qty, 1) OVER (ORDER BY order_date, id) AS prev_qty FROM orders WHERE status = 'delivered' ORDER BY order_date, id;
